marks.gloss_en: his derivation from Gen 38:20: here 'kid OF THE GOATS', so plain 'kid' is wider
R' Elazar: here it is 'kid of goats'; so wherever 'kid' is stated plainly, even a cow and a ewe are implied
שנאמר ומתו בו כי יחללוהו -- excluding teruma already desecrated
וסבר שמואל איסור חל על איסור? והאמר שמואל משום רבי אלעזר: an impure priest who ate impure teruma is not liable to death (an amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest)
Shmuel in R' Elazar's name: an impure priest who ate impure teruma is not liable to death
מדאיצטריכא לשמואל למימר ולא בחלב זכר -- it is the male that does not come into the category of mother; this one does, so it is forbidden
cooking in the milk of a kid that has not nursed: since it comes into the category of mother, it is forbidden
ולילף מיניה? -- let us learn from it [that every 'kid' is a goat]
another verse is written: 'the skins of the kids of the goats' (Gen 27:16) -- here 'kids of the goats', so plain 'kid' includes even cow and ewe
ולילף מיניה? -- [attacking the previous answer] let us learn from it [too]
they are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach
and any two verses that come as one do not teach
הניחא למאן דאמר אין מלמדין, אלא למאן דאמר מלמדין מאי איכא למימר? -- [attacking the previous answer]
two exclusions are written: 'izim', 'haizim'
הא תלתא גדי כתיבי ואנן שיתא דרשינן! -- three 'kid' are written and we expound six

Shmuel holds issur chal al issur, and fat and a dead animal come from one verse; blood is not 'kid'; the placenta is a mere secretion; two remain: one to include a fetus, one to exclude a non-kosher animal
Shmuel holds a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition, and the prohibitions of fat and of a dead animal come from one verse
איבעית אימא: in general it takes effect, and there it is different, for the Merciful One excluded with 'and die therein'
איבעית אימא: in general Shmuel holds it does not take effect, and here it is different, for the Merciful One included with 'kid'
ואיבעית אימא: this is his own [view], that is his teacher's
Shmuel: 'kid' -- to include fat
Shmuel: 'kid' -- to exclude blood
Shmuel: 'in its mother's milk' -- and not in the milk of a male
one who cooks forbidden fat in milk -- one says: he is flogged
no: all agree a prohibition does not take effect on a prohibition, and on eating all agree he is not flogged
